newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain one-year bills to set a record yield low.
newsitem.headline: Spain one-year bills to set a record yield low.

text.p: The Spanish Treasury is expected to set a fresh record low on the yields of one-year bills it will auction on Wednesday, analysts and dealers said.

The forecast is based on the level of the secondary market, where this maturity was trading on Tuesday at 6.50/6.53 percent. This will compare with a yield of 6.751 percent on the October 2 auction, just one day before the Bank of Spain cut its key money market rate by 50 basis points to 6.75 percent.
"On the secondary market the yields are trading around 6.50/6.55 percent -- where it is likely to see the new historic low at the auction tomorrow," a dealer said.
